text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Australian Tax Office is widening its crackdown on tax avoidance by the nation's richest people as it targets another 100 wealthy taxpayers this year. Taxation Commissioner Michael Carmody said the ATO is ready to ask for information on the tax arrangements of approximately 100 new targets. Page 1.

Independent Senator Mal Colston is at the centre of a row involving allegations of abuses of parliamentary entitlements. The allegations, made by former Colston staffer Andrew Hillard, claim that Senator Colston cashed in his parliamentary stamp allowance paid family members for work they did not do, and rorted travel-expense claims. Page 3.

An inquiry has been launched into a flying incident involving Dick Smith, the Federal Government's favoured candidate for the chairmanship of the troubled Civil Aviation Safety Authority. Smith defended the alleged breaches, claiming he was a victim of a vendetta by air traffic controllers and others within the aviation bureaucracy. Page 5.

THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government has warned Papua New Guinea that aid programs have been put at risk following the PNG Government's authorisation of a covert operation which uses foreign mercenaries against rebels on Bougainville. Canberra has also warned PNG that its international reputation and business dealings could be severely damaged if it saw the operation through. Page 1.

Australian air carrier Qantas has warned that the ongoing brawl between the Federal Government and the Civil Aviation Safety Authority has spilled over into the aviation industry, as Qantas managing director James Strong claimed air safety was being used s a political football. Page 1.

Communications Minister Senator Richard Alston has indicated that he is not satisfied with the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's explanations surrounding the national broadcasters telecast of an ACTU-sponsored program two weeks ago. Senator Alston poitedly declined to wholly accept the ABC's explanation of the telecast as the broadcaster argued it was in the "public interest". Page 1.

The Federal Government is considering a proposal which may see it extract a larger dividend from the one-third sale of Telstra to help fill the A$2-$3 billion Budget black hole. The Telstra board and Finance Department have met to discuss options on the poposal. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Attorney-General Geoff Shaw has called for an urgent national summit on legal aid funding cuts following calls by lawyers for a New South Wales man facing drug charges to argue that he be freed because he is no longer eligible for legal ai. Page 1.

Australia may suspend its A$320 million aid program to Papua New Guinea following a Port Moresby decision to employ mercenaries to strike at the rebel heartland in Bougainville. PNG plans to employ up to 150 African-based mercenaries to help train securit forces and mount an operation against the Bougainville Revolutionary Army. Page 1.

The New South Wales Government has launched a safety audit of amusement parks after the weekend death of eleven-year-old Shandy Lee Clare when a ride at the Rylstone-Kandos Country Show failed and caused a passenger chair to snap from the mounting. Report reveal that about 6.30 pm on Saturday night the ride - the Giant Octopus - broke, causing a chair containing the girl and two friends of the same age to crash to the ground. Shandy was killed instantly while the others sustained serious injuries. Page 3.

The Federal Government's plans for a shake-up of media ownership rules will have to face the test of the Senate with the Australian Democrats flagging a full Senate inquiry into the proposed changes. The Democrats' proposal follows revelations that the Oposition has decided to oppose any loosening of media ownership restrictions in the Senate. Page 3.
THE AGE

Relations between Australia and Papua New Guinea have deteriorated to a low point over the PNG Government's hiring of about 30 foreign mercenaries to assassinate rebel leaders on Bougainville. The Australian Government has threatened to review its aid prorams if the PNG Government goes ahead to use the mercenaries to escalate Bougainvillaea's nine-year-war. Page A1. --

Fourteen women in a country Victorian town have made allegations of sexual harassment - including rape - by police. The allegations first surfaced in the New South Wales Police Royal Commission two years ago, and now the Victorian Ombudsman's office has tken over investigations after the Victorian Police internal security unit made little progress into the matter. Page A1.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation has admitted it aired an ACTU-sponsored and externally-produced lecture of former Labor Prime Minister Gough Whitlam two weeks ago without anyone in the ABC's editorial management seeing it first. Page A3.

Queensland Police will officially treat threats to poison Arnott's biscuits as over if the person behind the treat fails to contact them by the close of business today. Qld Police released a statement saying they were waiting for contact from the extortioist and expected to receive something in the mail. Page A2.
